info.bio: El grupo Fun Lovin' Criminals se formó en 1993, cuando Huey trabajaba en un bar de la zona de Limelight en Nueva York. Fue allí donde conoció a Fast, que también trabajaba en el mismo local. En aquel momento, Fast formaba parte de un grupo tecno llamado Moses On Acid, que él mismo creó junto con el que más tarde sería el primer batería de Fun Lovin' Criminals, Steve-O. Al mismo tiempo, Huey solía pasar mucho tiempo tocando la guitarra al estilo blues, y pronto empezó a componer sus propias canciones junto con Fast.

scenes.name: Rap y hip hop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: A finales de los ochenta el «rockero» es una figura tan obsoleta como lo fue el cantante pop en 1956: tres revoluciones toman la música popular (el DJ como fuerza creativa, el hip hop y la fusión ciberpunk de industrial, metal y hardcore). En 1975 Kool Herc reinventa el breakbeat en el Bronx; el rap es una evolución del dub jamaicano. Sugar Hill Gang, Kurtis Blow, los «mensajes» de Grandmaster Flash, Afrika Bambaataa (el Leonardo del beatbox, inventor del «electro»), el tocadiscos como instrumento, Run-DMC, Tackhead, L.L. Cool J, Eric B & Rakim y Public Enemy (It Takes A Nation Of Millions, la obra maestra del hip hop). El gangsta rap (Schoolly D, NWA, Ice Cube, Dr Dre, 2Pac), Beastie Boys, las raperas (MC Lyte, Queen Latifah), De La Soul, A Tribe Called Quest, Cypress Hill; en Gran Bretaña, Art Of Noise.

podcast.title: Band Formation
podcast.body: The trio, fronted by Huey Morgan, formed in New York City. They began performing together at a club where they all worked, filling in when booked acts failed to appear. "They are a trio formed in New York City, fronted by Huey Morgan."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Continued Activity and Touring
podcast.body: Fun Lovin' Criminals remain an active entity, consistently touring, recording, and releasing new music. The band also commemorated the 20th anniversary of their seminal album, "Come Find Yourself," in 2016. "Fun Love and Criminals still exist. They continued to tour."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 1

podcast.title: Discovery and Record Deal
podcast.body: The band was noticed by a record executive during one of their fill-in performances at the club, leading to their signing with EMI. "On one of these occasions, they were noticed by a record guy who signed them to a deal with EMI."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 50 Biggest Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of All Time: Part 2 (40-31)

podcast.title: Huey Morgan's BBC Gig
podcast.body: Huey Morgan, who serves as the lead figure in Fun Lovin' Criminals, maintains a regular gig with the BBC, diversifying his musical and media engagements beyond his primary band role. "Lead Guy Huey Morgan has a regular gig with the BBC."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 1

podcast.title: Opening for U2
podcast.body: Their British fame also secured them an opening slot on U2's Pop Mart Tour in 1997. "The British fame also lighted them in opening slot on YouTube's Pop Mart Tour in 1997."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 50 Biggest Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of All Time: Part 2 (40-31)

podcast.title: Other Members' Projects
podcast.body: The two other members of Fun Lovin' Criminals are actively involved in various other musical projects, demonstrating their ongoing contributions to the music scene even while the band continues its operations. "While the other two members continue to work on various musical projects."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Great Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders of the 90s: Part 1

podcast.title: UK Stardom and Radio Career
podcast.body: Fun Lovin' Criminals achieved major success in Britain with multiple platinum and gold albums and numerous top 40 hits. This extensive fame led to Huey Morgan's transition to a career as a Radio DJ for the BBC. "The guy is a major star."
